Network-based analysis of side effect predictions for diphenhydramine and pemetrexed

Network-based analysis of side effect predictions for diphenhydramine and pemetrexed. (a) Baseline analysis for diphenhydramine, showing the recovery of a TP pathway phenotype, “hypertensive disease”, based on known drug-binding proteins. (b) Subnetwork for diphenhydramine after incorporating targets from ChEMBL, resulting in the recovery of both the baseline pathway phenotype, “hypertensive disease”, and a new TP pathway phenotype, “old myocardial infarction”. (c) Subnetwork for diphenhydramine with targets from PocketFEATURE, recovering both previous TP pathway phenotypes (“hypertensive disease” and “old myocardial infarction”) and identifying a newly defined TP pathway phenotype. (d) Analysis of pemetrexed, which had no TP pathway phenotypes in the baseline analysis but identified multiple new TP pathway phenotypes, including “genetic hypertension”, “thrombocytopenia 5”, and “neuropathy”, after integrating targets from New_DrugBank. A protein complex, which represents 37 proteins (12 of which are shown in this subnetwork), connects pemetrexed’s binding protein ALB to downstream pathways, influencing these newly identified pathway phenotypes
